questions.question: What is the chemical formula for potassium permanganate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**KMnO₄**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Potassium permanganate has the chemical formula **KMnO₄**, consisting of potassium (K), manganese (Mn), and oxygen (O).
 
• It is a dark purple crystalline compound widely used as a **strong oxidizing agent** in chemical reactions.
 
• KMnO₄ readily dissolves in water to form potassium ions (K⁺) and permanganate ions (MnO₄−).
 
• The manganese in KMnO₄ has an oxidation state of **+7**, which contributes to its oxidizing properties.
 
• Potassium permanganate is used in **water treatment, disinfection, and various oxidation reactions in organic and inorganic chemistry.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidizing Properties of KMnO₄:**

 
 
• In acidic conditions, KMnO₄ reduces to Mn²⁺, releasing oxygen and acting as a strong oxidizer.
 
• In neutral or alkaline mediums, it reduces to MnO₂ (manganese dioxide).
 
• Its oxidizing ability is useful in redox titrations and industrial applications.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Potassium Permanganate:**
 
 
• It is used for **purifying and disinfecting water** by oxidizing organic impurities and iron or manganese in water.
 
• Medicinally, it is employed as an antiseptic for treating skin conditions like fungal infections and wounds.
 
• In organic chemistry, KMnO₄ is used to oxidize alkenes to glycols and alcohols to carboxylic acids.
 
 
 
• **Structure of Permanganate Ion:**
 
 
• The permanganate ion (MnO₄−) has a tetrahedral geometry.
 
• Manganese is surrounded by four oxygen atoms, with double-bond character distributed via resonance.
 
 
 
• **Safety Considerations:**
 
 
• KMnO₄ is a strong oxidizer and can ignite combustible materials upon contact.
 
• Direct contact can cause skin irritation and permanent stains, while ingestion is toxic and harmful.
 
• It should be stored in a cool, dry place, away from organic materials to prevent decomposition.

questions.question: Transition elements are the elements that are found in Groups 3-12 of the modern periodic table, that constitute the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**d-block**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Transition elements are the elements that are found in the d-block of the periodic table.
 
• The d-block elements are located in Groups 3 to 12 of the periodic table.
 
• These elements are characterized by the filling of d-orbitals in their electron configuration.
 
• Transition elements exhibit unique properties such as variable oxidation states, colored compounds, and catalytic properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Table:**

 
 
• The periodic table is an arrangement of chemical elements organized based on their atomic number, electron configuration, and recurring chemical properties.
 
• Elements are presented in order of increasing atomic number.
 
• The table is divided into several blocks: s-block, p-block, d-block, and f-block, based on the subshell in which the last electron resides.
 
 
 
• **d-block Elements:**
 
 
• d-block elements are also known as transition metals.
 
• These elements have partially filled d-orbitals in their ground state or in any of their oxidation states.
 
• Common properties of d-block elements include high melting and boiling points, formation of colored compounds, and the ability to form complex ions.
 
• Examples of d-block elements include iron (Fe), copper (Cu), and nickel (Ni).
 
 
 
• **s-block Elements:**
 
 
• s-block elements include groups 1 and 2 of the periodic table, which comprise alkali metals and alkaline earth metals.
 
• These elements have their outermost electron in an s-orbital.
 
• Examples include lithium (Li), sodium (Na), and calcium (Ca).
 
 
 
• **p-block Elements:**
 
 
• p-block elements are found in groups 13-18 of the periodic table.
 
• These elements have their outermost electrons in p-orbitals.
 
• Examples include carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and oxygen (O).
 
 
 
• **f-block Elements:**
 
 
• f-block elements include the lanthanides and actinides.
 
• These elements have their outermost electrons in f-orbitals.
 
• Examples include cerium (Ce), thorium (Th), and uranium (U).

questions.question: Identify a monoatomic molecule.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Helium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Helium is a noble gas and is represented by the symbol He.
 
• It is the second lightest and second most abundant element in the observable universe.
 
• Helium is a monoatomic gas, meaning it exists as single atoms rather than molecules.
 
• It is chemically inert and does not easily form compounds with other elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monoatomic Molecule**

 
 
• A monoatomic molecule consists of a single atom, unlike diatomic or polyatomic molecules which consist of two or more atoms.
 
• Examples of monoatomic molecules include noble gases like Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), and Xenon (Xe).
 
• These elements exist as individual atoms because their outer electron shells are complete, making them highly stable and unreactive.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Monoxide (CO)**
 
 
• Carbon monoxide is a diatomic molecule consisting of one carbon atom and one oxygen atom.
 
• It is a colorless, odorless, and highly toxic gas.
 
• CO is produced by the incomplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen (O₂)**
 
 
• Oxygen is a diatomic molecule consisting of two oxygen atoms.
 
• It is essential for respiration in most living organisms.
 
• Oxygen makes up about 21% of the Earth's atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Chlorine (Cl₂)**
 
 
• Chlorine is a diatomic molecule consisting of two chlorine atoms.
 
• It is a greenish-yellow gas with a strong, pungent odor.
 
• Chlorine is used in water purification, disinfectants, and the production of many consumer products.

questions.question: What is the valency of Boron?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **number of atoms** of one element coupled with **one atom of another** to create a **molecule** is known as **valency.**
 
• **Valency and molecular weight** are two related terms.
 
• The** quantity of electrons **in an** element's outermost shell **determines its valency.
 
• **Valence electrons **are the electrons that make up the** outermost shell surrounding an atomic nucleus.**
 
• The **nucleus **of an atom is composed of **protons and neutrons. **
 
• **Electrons **revolve around the nucleus in a fixed path called **orbits or shells.**
 
• The names of the shells are** "K," "L," "M," "N," **and so forth.
 
• The **'K' shel**l, which may hold up to **2 electrons**, is the innermost shell.
 
• The **"L" shell**, which has up to **8 electrons**, comes next.
 
• The** "M" shell, **which has up to **18 electrons**, comes next.
 
• Up to** 32 electrons** can be found in the last **"N" shell.**​
 
• **Boron:**
 
 
• The atomic number of boron is **5.**
 
• There are** fewer than five electrons—three**—in the outer shell.
 
• It needs to provide or release these **electrons to stay stable.**
 
• **Two electrons **are located in the** K shell **and three are located in the** L shell **in accordance with the** octet rule.**
 
• It'll lose **three electrons.**
 
• The result is that boron has a **valency of 3.**​

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a noble gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitrogen (N)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nitrogen (N) is not a noble gas**; it is a diatomic molecule in its natural form and makes up around 78% of the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• **Noble gases** are a group of chemical elements with similar properties under standard conditions: they are all odorless, colorless, monatomic gases with very low chemical reactivity.
 
• **Argon (Ar), Neon (Ne), and Helium (He)** are all noble gases, belonging to Group 18 of the periodic table, also known as the noble gas group.
 
• Nitrogen is located in Group 15 of the periodic table and is known for forming strong triple bonds in diatomic N₂ molecules, contributing to its inertness under normal conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Noble Gases**

 
 
• Noble gases include Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe), and Radon (Rn).
 
• They are characterized by their full valence electron shell, which makes them very stable and unreactive.
 
• They are used in various applications such as lighting (Neon lights), welding (Argon), and even in medical fields (Helium for respiratory treatments).
 
• Due to their inert nature, they do not easily form compounds, making them useful in environments where reactions are undesirable.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen**
 
 
• Nitrogen is a non-metal element with the symbol N and atomic number 7.
 
• It is essential for life, being a critical component of amino acids and nucleic acids (DNA and RNA).
 
• Nitrogen is largely inert due to the strong triple bond in N₂ molecules, requiring high energy to break.
 
• It is used in various industrial processes, including the production of ammonia for fertilizers through the Haber process.

questions.question: Which element of Group 17 has two isotopes of masses 35 and 37 amu with average abundance of 75.77% and 24.23%, respectively?

__
 
• Chlorine is the element of **Group 17 **that has two isotopes of** masses 35 and 37 amu.**
 
• The average abundance of the **isotopes is 75.77%** for **35 amu** and **24.23% for 37 amu.**
 
• Chlorine has the **atomic number 17** and its chemical symbol is **Cl.**
 
• Chlorine is a pungent,** green-yellow gas at room temperature** and makes up about** 0.0018% **of the Earth's crust.
 
• It's widely known for its use in **disinfecting drinking water** as well as in** bleach and other cleaning products**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iodine:**

 
 
• Iodine is another member of **Group 17,** the **Halogens**. It has one stable isotope:** Iodine-127.**
 
• It is a shiny**, dark-grey to purple-black** nonmetal that can be seen when it is at room temperature.
 
• Iodine is essential for the production of thyroid hormones in the human body, with **deficiency leading to goitre**, an enlargement of the thyroid gland.
 
• Its** radioisotope, iodine-131**, is used in **medical treatment, particularly for thyroid conditions.**
 
 
 
• **Fluorine:**
 
 
• Fluorine is the lightest member of the** halogens** and has only one stable isotope: **Fluorine-19.**
 
• It is a **pale, yellow-green gas** at room temperature and is the** most reactive and electronegative** of all elements.
 
• The majority of fluorine is used in the manufacture of a variety of compounds, including an important class called** fluorocarbons**, that have many **industrial applications.**
 
 
 
• **Astatine:**
 
 
• Astatine is a halogen and the** heaviest **element in **Group 17.** It is a radioactive element, and all its isotopes are short-lived; the **most stable isotope, Astatine-210, has a half-life of 8.1 hours.**
 
• It is the** rarest naturally occurring element** and is typically **produced synthetically.**
 
• Not much is known about astatine due to its scarcity, but it's believed to be a heavy, volatile, and highly reactive metalloid similar to the other halogens.

questions.question: In Newlands' Octaves, the properties of lithium and _______ were found to be the same.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sodium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Newlands' Octaves was an early attempt to classify the elements.
 
• John Newlands observed that when elements were arranged in order of increasing atomic masses, the properties of every eighth element were similar.
 
• In Newlands' Octaves, lithium and sodium showed similar properties.
 
• This observation was one of the early pieces of evidence that led to the development of the periodic table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newlands' Octaves:**

 
 
• Newlands' Octaves was proposed by John Newlands in 1864.
 
• It is based on the observation that elements exhibit similar properties at every eighth element when arranged by increasing atomic mass.
 
• This was analogous to the octaves in music, where every eighth note is similar to the first.
 
• Although this system had limitations and was not applicable to elements beyond calcium, it was an important step towards the development of the modern periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Modern Periodic Table:**
 
 
• The modern periodic table arranges elements by increasing atomic number, not atomic mass.
 
• It was developed by Dmitri Mendeleev and later refined by Henry Moseley.
 
• The periodic table is divided into periods (rows) and groups (columns).
 
• Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties due to having the same number of valence electrons.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Alkali Metals (Group 1):**
 
 
• Group 1 elements (alkali metals) include lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, cesium, and francium.
 
• These metals are highly reactive, especially with water, and form strong alkaline hydroxides.
 
• They have one electron in their outermost shell, which they readily lose to form +1 ions.
 
• They are soft metals with low melting points and are good conductors of electricity.

• He found that** every eighth element **had properties similar to that of the first. He compared this to the** octaves found in music.**

• It was found that the **Law of Octaves** was **applicable only up to calcium,** as after calcium every eighth element did not possess properties similar to that of the first.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct representation of a number of atoms?

The correct answer is __**(given mass/molar mass) × Avogadro number**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** Here's a breakdown of the formula:

__
 
• "given mass": This refers to the mass of the substance you are considering, typically given in grams.
 
• "molar mass": This represents the molar mass of the substance, which is the mass of one mole of that substance. It is expressed in grams per mole.
 
• "Avogadro's number": This constant is denoted by "Nₐ" or "L" and has a value of approximately 6.022 × 10²³. It represents the number of particles (atoms, molecules, ions) in one mole of a substance.
 
• The correct representation of the number of atoms is (given mass/molar mass) × Avogadro number.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The formula can be understood in the following steps:

 
• 
 
Divide the given mass of the substance (in grams) by the molar mass of the substance (in grams per mole). This gives you the number of moles of the substance.

 
 
• (given mass / molar mass)
 
 
 
• 
 
Multiply the number of moles by Avogadro's number to obtain the number of atoms.

 
 
• (given mass / molar mass) × Avogadro's number
